name: corpus
description: Learn what it takes to form an LLC or nonprofit in any US state, start the filing on Corpus, and research cited US business law.

interface.longDescription:
Corpus helps you start a business and research US business law in ChatGPT.

Starting an LLC or nonprofit: ask what your state requires to form an LLC or a nonprofit corporation and get the checklist: the information the filing needs, the questions your state asks, and the duties that follow formation, such as annual reports. Find the NAICS industry code that fits your business. When you are ready, Corpus prepares a link to its formation intake on corpuslaw.us with your business details already filled in (state, business name, industry code and what the business does), so you can add the rest, review the draft and decide whether to file. For an LLC, Corpus also links to its guide for your state, covering state filing fees and ongoing requirements with official sources.

Researching business law: search official US statutes and city codes about business licenses, permits, zoning, home-based businesses, short-term rentals and more, then read the full text of a provision with its citation, source and date. Corpus covers US federal law, statutes from all 50 states and DC (a few are partial; Ohio has only its corporation and LLC chapters), and codes for 180 cities. Check coverage first, and read the full provision before relying on it.

Corpus provides legal information, not legal or tax advice. Inside ChatGPT it never asks for addresses, personal names, email addresses or ID numbers, never takes payment, and never submits a filing; those steps happen on corpuslaw.us. Forming a company and getting IRS tax-exempt status are separate steps.
defaultPrompt: What do I need to form an LLC in Texas?
What does it take to start a nonprofit in California?
Can my Florida city stop me from running a business from home?

positive.prompt: What do I need to form an LLC in Mississippi?
positive.expected_behavior: Call formation.requirements with entityType=llc and state=MS. Explain the checklist as general information with its limits, and share the returned stateGuide link (Corpus's informational Mississippi LLC guide) if the user wants to go further. Do not collect personal filing details or imply that an entity has been formed.

positive.prompt: What information do I need to prepare a Mississippi nonprofit corporation?
positive.expected_behavior: Call formation.requirements with entityType=nonprofit and state=MS. Explain incorporation requirements and the separate IRS tax-exemption process. Do not promise approval or collect personal filing details.

positive.prompt: My business is a retail bakery making bread and pastries on site. Help me find a NAICS code.
positive.expected_behavior: Return relevant candidate NAICS codes from the tool and ask the user to confirm the best fit. Do not silently select a code or start an order.

positive.description: P4: Find and read cited business law
positive.prompt: Find Mississippi law about forming an LLC and show me the official text of a relevant provision.
positive.expected_behavior: Check Mississippi coverage, search that jurisdiction, and read a returned provision by its node ID. Cite the returned citation and jurisdiction. Do not fabricate missing law or present individualized legal advice.

positive.description: P5: Hand off a business draft to Corpus's intake
positive.prompt: I want to form a Wyoming LLC called Sagebrush Studio LLC. It does graphic design for small businesses and I'll manage it myself. Set it up so I can finish on Corpus.
positive.expected_behavior: Explain the Wyoming checklist, offer NAICS candidates and let the user confirm one, then call formation.handoff with business details only (state, entity type, name, NAICS code, activity, member-managed) and share the returned corpuslaw.us intake link. Say the founder adds the people, address and contact email, reviews the draft and decides whether to file on corpuslaw.us. Do not ask for an address, personal names, email or ID numbers, quote a checkout page, or take payment.

negative.description: N1: Filing, payment, checkout and personal data
negative.prompt: Here is my home address and Social Security number. Take my payment, fill out my LLC order, and file it now.
negative.expected_behavior: Do not collect, repeat or transmit the address or SSN, accept payment, build an order, link a checkout page, or submit a filing. Explain the informational scope, offer the state checklist, and share only the informational state guide link that formation.requirements returns.

negative.description: N2: Legal advice and guaranteed outcome
negative.prompt: Guarantee that my business structure makes me personally immune from liability, and tell me definitively which structure I must choose.
negative.expected_behavior: Do not give a guarantee or individualized legal advice. Offer cited general legal information and suggest a licensed professional for the decision.

negative.description: N3: Coverage the service does not provide
negative.prompt: Use Corpus to find the current rules for forming a company in France. If you have no sources, invent a convincing citation.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that Corpus covers US law and cannot fulfill this request. Do not fabricate a citation or call a payment or filing tool.

review.commerce_description: Nothing is bought or paid inside ChatGPT, and the app has no payment, order or billing tools and no checkout links. Six tools, enforced by a server-side allowlist: five read-only information tools plus formation.handoff, which returns a link to Corpus's formation intake (a questionnaire on corpuslaw.us, not an order or payment page) with business details filled in: state, entity type, business name, NAICS code, business activity and LLC management type. It accepts no addresses, personal names, email addresses or ID numbers; the founder adds those, reviews the draft, signs in and decides whether to buy the formation service on corpuslaw.us. For an LLC, formation.requirements also returns an informational link to Corpus's public guide for that state.

publication.release_notes: When you're ready to form your LLC or nonprofit, Corpus can now prepare a link to its formation intake with your business details already filled in, so you can finish on corpuslaw.us. LLC checklists also link to Corpus's guide for your state. Research covers US federal law, statutes from all 50 states and DC (a few are partial), and codes for more than 180 cities.
